title: The vegan fast food trend
paragraphs: There are around 600,000 vegans in the UK, according to The Vegan Society. That's just over 1% of the population – an amount expected to increase to 25% by 2025. And if there's one type of food that Brits love, it's fast food. True, it's not the most nutritious, but there's nothing quite like the crunch of crispy chips, or that first big bite into a juicy hamburger. People in the UK love junk food so much that there was a 34% increase in the number of fast food outlets from 2010 to 2018, according to the Office for National Statistics. It's no surprise, then, that vegan fast food is also on the rise.

Vegan fast food has become big business. At Just Eat, an online food delivery company, vegan orders more than doubled in 2018, a spokesperson told the BBC. Greggs, a chain of high-street bakeries, named its vegan sausage roll the 'fastest-selling product in six years'. And big franchises such as McDonald's and KFC have announced meat-free chicken nuggets to come in the future.

What's driving this popularity? Katrina Fox, founder of Vegan Business Media, believes it's the result of social media and the breaking down of stereotypes. "Vegan food is no longer seen as a bit of lettuce and lentils – you can eat pretty much anything," she told the BBC. It's also claimed that there are health benefits. John Marulanda, owner of Mooshies - a vegan burger bar in London – wants to implement "a change to a healthy version of fast food." Something, he claims, that comes as a result of the inherent nutritional value of the ingredients they use.

But, is vegan fast food actually healthy? Azmina Govindji of the British Dietetic Association says "not to assume" that is the case. "It's fine if those products have got vitamin B12, iodine or calcium added to them… but they can still be fried, it can still have lots of creamy, fatty sauces and lots of salt."

Given the current growth in orders, the trend for vegan fast food isn't likely to disappear any time soon. Health-wise, it may not be any more nourishing than regular fast food, but for many, the lack of animal suffering involved in the process is a big plus.

vocabulary.entry: vegan /ˈviːɡən/ n. 素食主义者（不食用任何动物产品，包括肉、蛋、奶）
vocabulary.example: She has been a vegan for five years and feels much healthier.
vocabulary.translation: 她已经做了五年素食主义者，感觉健康多了。

vocabulary.entry: nutritious /njuˈtrɪʃəs/ adj. 有营养的；滋养的
vocabulary.example: Fresh fruit and vegetables are highly nutritious.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜水果和蔬菜营养价值很高。

vocabulary.entry: crunch /krʌntʃ/ n. （食物的）酥脆声；咔嚓声
vocabulary.example: I love the crunch of toast for breakfast.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢早餐时烤面包的酥脆口感。

vocabulary.entry: fast food outlet /ˌfɑːst fuːd ˈaʊtlet/ 快餐门店
vocabulary.example: There are several fast food outlets near the train station.
vocabulary.translation: 火车站附近有好几家快餐门店。

vocabulary.entry: on the rise /ɒn ðə raɪz/ 正在兴起；日益增加
vocabulary.example: Interest in renewable energy is on the rise.
vocabulary.translation: 人们对可再生能源的兴趣正在日益增加。

vocabulary.entry: big business /ˌbɪɡ ˈbɪznəs/ 大生意；热门行业
vocabulary.example: Online education has become big business in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来，在线教育已成为一门热门行业。

vocabulary.entry: online food delivery /ˌɒnlaɪn fuːd dɪˈlɪvəri/ 在线外卖
vocabulary.example: Online food delivery services are very popular among busy workers.
vocabulary.translation: 在线外卖服务在忙碌的上班族中非常受欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: chain /tʃeɪn/ n. 连锁商店；连锁店
vocabulary.example: This coffee chain has branches in over 50 countries.
vocabulary.translation: 这家咖啡连锁店在50多个国家设有分店。

vocabulary.entry: high-street /ˌhaɪ ˈstriːt/ adj. （英国）商业街的；繁华街道的
vocabulary.example: She works in a high-street clothing store.
vocabulary.translation: 她在一家商业街的服装店工作。

vocabulary.entry: franchise /ˈfræntʃaɪz/ n. 特许经营店；连锁品牌
vocabulary.example: He bought a franchise of a famous fast food brand.
vocabulary.translation: 他买下了一个知名快餐品牌的特许经营权。

vocabulary.entry: meat-free /miːt friː/ adj. 无肉的；素食的
vocabulary.example: The restaurant offers a variety of meat-free dishes.
vocabulary.translation: 这家餐厅提供多种无肉菜肴。

vocabulary.entry: drive /draɪv/ v. 推动；促使
vocabulary.example: Technological innovation is driving the development of the industry.
vocabulary.translation: 技术创新正在推动该行业的发展。

vocabulary.entry: stereotype /ˈsteriətaɪp/ n. 刻板印象；固有观念
vocabulary.example: We need to break down the stereotype that women are not good at science.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要打破女性不擅长科学的刻板印象。

vocabulary.entry: lettuce /ˈletɪs/ n. 生菜；莴苣
vocabulary.example: I added some lettuce and tomatoes to my sandwich.
vocabulary.translation: 我在三明治里加了些生菜和西红柿。

vocabulary.entry: lentil /ˈlentɪl/ n. 小扁豆
vocabulary.example: Lentils are a good source of protein for vegans.
vocabulary.translation: 小扁豆是素食主义者获取蛋白质的良好来源。

vocabulary.entry: implement /ˈɪmplɪment/ v. 实施；推行
vocabulary.example: The company plans to implement a new training program next month.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司计划下个月推行一项新的培训计划。

vocabulary.entry: inherent /ɪnˈhɪərənt/ adj. 固有的；内在的

vocabulary.translation: 这个计划存在一些我们需要考虑的内在风险。

vocabulary.entry: dietetic association /ˌdaɪəˈtetɪk əˌsəʊsiˈeɪʃn/ 饮食协会
vocabulary.example: The British Dietetic Association provides advice on healthy eating.
vocabulary.translation: 英国饮食协会提供健康饮食方面的建议。

vocabulary.entry: iodine /ˈaɪədiːn/ n. 碘
vocabulary.example: Iodine is an essential mineral for thyroid function.
vocabulary.translation: 碘是甲状腺功能所需的重要矿物质。

vocabulary.entry: calcium /ˈkælsiəm/ n. 钙
vocabulary.example: Milk and cheese are rich in calcium.
vocabulary.translation: 牛奶和奶酪富含钙质。

vocabulary.entry: nourishing /ˈnʌrɪʃɪŋ/ adj. 滋养的；有营养的
vocabulary.example: Homemade soup is warm and nourishing.
vocabulary.translation: 自制的汤温暖又滋养。

vocabulary.entry: plus /plʌs/ n. 优势；好处
vocabulary.example: The location of the apartment is a big plus for commuters.
vocabulary.translation: 这套公寓的位置对通勤者来说是一大优势。

sentences.chinese: 在线外卖平台Just Eat的发言人向英国广播公司表示，2018年该平台的素食订单量增长了一倍多。

sentences.english: Greggs, a chain of high-street bakeries, named its vegan sausage roll the 'fastest-selling product in six years'.
sentences.chinese: 繁华商业街连锁烘焙品牌格雷格斯（Greggs）将其推出的素食香肠卷称为“六年来最畅销产品”。

sentences.english: And big franchises such as McDonald's and KFC have announced meat-free chicken nuggets to come in the future.
sentences.chinese: 麦当劳、肯德基等大型连锁品牌也已宣布，未来将推出无肉鸡块。
是什么催生了素食快餐的流行？

sentences.english: Katrina Fox, founder of Vegan Business Media, believes it's the result of social media and the breaking down of stereotypes.
sentences.chinese: 素食商业媒体（Vegan Business Media）创始人卡特里娜·福克斯认为，这得益于社交媒体的推动以及刻板印象的打破。

sentences.english: "Vegan food is no longer seen as a bit of lettuce and lentils – you can eat pretty much anything," she told the BBC.
sentences.chinese: 她向英国广播公司表示：“素食不再被看作只有生菜和小扁豆——你几乎可以吃到任何想吃的东西。”

sentences.english: It's also claimed that there are health benefits.
sentences.chinese: 还有人称，素食快餐对健康有益。

sentences.english: John Marulanda, owner of Mooshies - a vegan burger bar in London – wants to implement "a change to a healthy version of fast food." Something, he claims, that comes as a result of the inherent nutritional value of the ingredients they use.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦素食汉堡店Mooshies的老板约翰·马鲁兰达希望“推动快餐向健康化转型”，他表示，这得益于他们所使用食材本身的营养价值。

sentences.english: But, is vegan fast food actually healthy?
sentences.chinese: 但素食快餐真的健康吗？

sentences.english: Azmina Govindji of the British Dietetic Association says "not to assume" that is the case.
sentences.chinese: 英国饮食协会的阿兹米娜·戈文德吉表示，“不能想当然地”认为事实就是如此。

sentences.english: "It's fine if those products have got vitamin B12, iodine or calcium added to them… but they can still be fried, it can still have lots of creamy, fatty sauces and lots of salt."
sentences.chinese: “如果这些产品添加了维生素B12、碘或钙，那当然是好事……但它们仍可能经过油炸，可能含有大量奶油状高脂酱料，且含盐量不低。”

sentences.english: Given the current growth in orders, the trend for vegan fast food isn't likely to disappear any time soon.
sentences.chinese: 从目前订单的增长趋势来看，素食快餐的热潮短期内不太可能消退。

sentences.english: Health-wise, it may not be any more nourishing than regular fast food, but for many, the lack of animal suffering involved in the process is a big plus.
sentences.chinese: 就健康而言，它或许并不比普通快餐更具营养价值，但对许多人来说，生产过程中不涉及动物受苦，这便是一大优势。
